title: Lighthouse quarter check-in & sprint notes
content:
Context: Quick personal scratchpad for the quarter — mix of numerical check-ins, hypothesis notes for experiments, and a lightweight retro. Not polished. Used to prep 1:1 and the eng quarterly sync.

Summary goals (Q1 2026 intent) — personal slice aligned to team OKRs:
- O1: Improve production latency profile for hosted API (measurable): lower p95 across common models by 12% while keeping cost/1M tokens within -3% budget.
- O2: Reduce customer-visible fallbacks by making routing + cache heuristics smarter (target: 30% fewer fallbacks on busiest routes).
- O3: Ship two lightweight tooling improvements for rollout observability (per-route health + token-level cost breakdown in console).

Why these?
- Latency tail is the thing customers notice and it compounds SLO violations. If I can nudge p95 down it's high ROI.
- Fallbacks = bad UX + noisy support tickets. We can mitigate by more aggressive model variant selection and a micro-caching policy.
- Observability features unblock PMs and SREs to make better decisions and reduce manual triage.

Current numbers (last 2 weeks snapshot):
- Baseline (production-average across top 10 routes): p50=85ms, p95=420ms, p99=860ms.
- Cost per 1M tokens (hosted): $46.8 (encoder+decoder blended).
- Fallback incidence on top 10 routes: 4.8% -> target <3.5%.
- Rollout observability tickets created by customers last 30d: 12 (mostly asks for per-route token cost).

What I did last sprint (concrete):
- Experimented with an aggressive KV prefix cache on route /chat-instant — small throughput tradeoff, p95 down 18% on synthetic replay. Need production canary. (linked: jira:INF-342)
- Added lightweight token-cost metric to local dev console; demoed to Ivy on 2026-02-10. Feedback: show 7-day trend + delta from baseline.
- Paired with Samir on routing policy A/B config; we created a canary rollout plan for dedicated customers (PR: runtime#891).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does the prefix cache harm cold-start scenarios for rare long-context requests? Quick replay didn't show degradation but production patterns differ.
- Can we automate a safety valve that backs off cache aggression for routes with high variance?
- How to measure perceived user impact (support tickets are a lagging indicator). Idea: lightweight on-request feedback for a small subset of routes (opt-in).

Hypotheses to test (priority order):
1) Aggressive prefix caching reduces p95 without increasing overall cost for steady-state traffic. Metric: delta p95 and delta cost/1M tokens over 7-day canary windows.
2) Latency-aware routing (route-level expected-latency estimate) reduces fallback incidence by >20% with <2% increase in avg token cost.
3) Per-route cost visibility will cut observability tickets by 30% within 6 weeks because customers self-serve.

Mini experiment plan for #1 (canary):
- Canary group: two low-latency regions + 5% traffic on route /chat-instant for one week.
- Monitoring: p50/p95/p99, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, token-cost, cold-start latency for long sequences.
- Rollback policy: auto-roll back if p99 increases by >10% or error rate spikes >0.2% above baseline.

Retrospective notes (what went well / what to fix):
- Went well: Faster iteration on local tooling enabled an easier demo and tighter feedback loop with Ivy. Samir and I kept canary plan light.
- Fix: I under-specified the observability dashboard mock for PM review — added rework to next sprint. Also need automated synthetic replay pipelines; manual replays are slow and brittle.

Personal cadence items (weekly check-in template I used):
- 1-sentence outcome last week
- 3 numbers I care about (p95 delta, cost delta, fallbacks%)
- Blockers (1-2) + ask for help
- Next actions for the week (3 items)

This week's quick check (2026-02-21):
- Outcome: Confirmed synthetic replays show p95 improvement with cache variant; canary scheduled for 2 days.
- Numbers to watch: p95 target for canary <= 350ms; cost change <= +1.5%
- Blockers: Need infra approval for canary resource reservation; also need one more engineer to monitor the canary dashboard during business hours.
- Next actions: (1) Ping infra and get reservation (due 2026-02-22), (2) finish automated rollback hook (Samir collaborating), (3) create short customer-facing note for dedicated customers about expected behavior during canary.

Parking lot / ideas (non-urgent):
- Small UX experiment: let a customer opt-in to a "latency-preferred" profile that prefers faster model variants with price delta shown up-front.
- Run a short user-survey embedded in the console to measure perceived responsiveness for routes with and without cache.
- Internal doc: playbook for interpreting token-cost anomalies (map common causes -> triage steps).

1:1 talking points for next meeting with manager (quick bullets):
- Canary readiness and rollback safeguards (ask for sign-off window)
- Tradeoffs: near-term p95 improvement vs. potential cold-start regressions; proposed safety valve approach
- Capacity ask: reserve 1 T4x nightly slot for stress replays for the next 3 weeks

Notes to self: keep entries short, timestamped; capture exact metric queries for repeatability (promql saved queries). When demoing, show both absolute numbers and change vs baseline.

---
History: created as quick scratchpad Nov 2025; evolved into active canary plan Feb 2026.
